en.title: Spider-Man Director Utterly Baffled by Wonder Man Cancellation
en.summary: Despite the massive success of his latest Marvel film, director Destin Daniel Cretton is clueless as to why his upcoming Disney+ series, Wonder Man, was abruptly canceled. The move has left creators and fans alike scratching their heads.
en.body:
The Marvel Cinematic Universe is currently celebrating the monumental success of **Spider-Man: Brand New Day**, a film that has shattered box office records and revitalized audience enthusiasm for the franchise. However, this triumphant moment is shadowed by a perplexing decision from Disney and Marvel: the cancellation of the highly anticipated **Wonder Man** series, co-created by the very director behind **Spider-Man: Brand New Day**, **Destin Daniel Cretton**. The news arrived as a shockwave, particularly given that production was gearing up and schedules were being cleared for an imminent writers' room start.

**Destin Daniel Cretton** himself has expressed profound confusion and disappointment regarding the sudden axing. He revealed in interviews that the decision came from higher up, even suggesting that **Kevin Feige** was also a proponent of the show and would have greenlit it if it were solely his call. The exact reasoning remains a closely guarded secret, with Disney opting not to share specifics with the creative team. This lack of transparency is particularly frustrating for **Cretton**, who lauded the series' potential and praised star **Yahya Abdul-Mateen II** as "the fucking best." The situation is a stark reminder of the opaque business of streaming, where even critically and commercially promising projects can be pulled without clear explanation.

## A Creative Vision Left in Limbo

**Andrew Guest**, the co-creator of **Wonder Man** alongside **Cretton**, elaborated on the abruptness of the cancellation in a TikTok video, describing it as a "rug pull." He confirmed that the writers' room was set to convene that very week, and production was scheduled to commence early the following year. The internal decision, made by Disney and Marvel executives, was that the show "didn't make sense for them," a rationale that starkly contrasts with previous affirmations of the project's viability just months prior. This sudden reversal leaves **Cretton** and **Guest**, along with the dedicated fanbase, in a state of bewilderment, questioning the strategic shifts within the studio that led to such a drastic and seemingly inexplicable decision.

## The Fan Fallout

For dedicated fans of the MCU and **Wonder Man**, this cancellation is a bitter pill to swallow. The series promised a unique blend of humor and heart, exploring the life of actor Simon Williams as he navigates his career and superhero alter ego. With **Destin Daniel Cretton** at the helm, fresh off the success of **Spider-Man: Brand New Day**, expectations were sky-high. The lack of a clear explanation fuels speculation and frustration within the online community, with many questioning the studio's priorities and the value placed on creative vision versus opaque streaming metrics. The outpouring of support for **Cretton** and the **Wonder Man** team underscores the deep disappointment felt by those who were eagerly anticipating this new chapter in the MCU.

## What's Next

While **Wonder Man** is officially off the table, **Destin Daniel Cretton** remains a key figure within Marvel Studios, and fans will undoubtedly be watching his future projects closely. Details regarding any potential reassurances or new assignments for the creative team involved with **Wonder Man** have not yet been announced.

content_raw: Showing how much they appreciate his work on Spider-Man: Brand New Day , the first unqualified Marvel movie success since Deadpool & Wolverine , Disney canceled Wonder-Man , the TV series co-created by Spidey director Destin Daniel Cretton. The news was a surprise, arriving on the eve of Marvel’s Brand New Day , which would go on to earn $1 billion in about four days. Cretton’s co-creator, Andrew Guest, explained in a TikTok video that the show’s axing was more of a rug pull. “Schedules were cleared,” he said. “The writers’ room was supposed to start this week. The production was supposed to begin early next year, and there was a decision made internally between Disney and Marvel that this didn’t make sense for them, even though a few months ago it did.” It’s strange to say the least, but Disney is keeping its streaming numbers under its Mickey hat and won’t even share the reason for the cancellation with Cretton. Speaking to The Wrap , Cretton expressed his love for the series and its star, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II (“the fucking best”), who earned an Emmy nod for the show. However, he’s as much in the dark as the rest of us regarding the sudden about-face on the show. Apparently, the call came from above Kevin Feige. “If it were up to me, we would be making that show,” Cretton says. “And I do believe that if–and I know this sounds weird–but if it were up to Kevin [Feige], we would be doing that show. And I’m just talking, I don’t fully understand the business of streaming, but if the business was right, we would be making that show because I know [Feige] loves that show as much as I do. It’s a bummer. I’m heartbroken about it. But I need to fully understand the why.” Though some online have suggested that this is all a marketing stunt for a Wonder Man movie, that’s even more unlikely than a second season at this point. Cretton, for his part, says the prospect of a movie is an “interesting question,” one he can’t answer because Disney won’t share its streaming data with him, so he doesn’t “clearly know if it’s a success or not.”  On the strength of strong reviews, positive word of mouth, and supposedly solid streaming numbers (but apparently not solid enough), Wonder Man had been greenlit for season two last spring. After the cancellation, Abdul-Mateen II released a characteristically chill response. “That’s life, right? Everything will shake out,” the star wrote on Instagram. “I’m glad we got to be a part of something cool. Thank you for watching… And uhh… See you at the EMMYS.”
